mainTopic: Why the משנה of שנים אוחזין needs both cases, and whether it fits בן ננס and סומכוס
overview: The גמרא explains why the משנה teaches two cases, a found item and a purchase. Each case has its own excuse a person might use to grab dishonestly, so neither case could be learned from the other. It then asks how a purchase dispute could happen at all. The answer is that the seller took money from both people and forgot which payment he truly accepted. Next, the גמרא asks whether our משנה disagrees with בן ננס, who objects to oaths where one must be false. It answers that here both oaths could be true, since the two may have lifted the item together. Finally, it tests our משנה against סומכוס, who splits doubtful money without an oath. It defends the משנה first by limiting his rule to שמא ושמא, then by limiting it to cases of דררא דממונא. A new קל וחומר against that last answer begins and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: If only the found-item case were taught
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה taught only מציאה, we would think the oath applies only there. A finder can easily excuse grabbing half, but a buyer cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the משנה had taught only the case of a found item, I would have said: only with a found item did the רבנן put an oath on him. That is because there he can excuse himself and say, 'My friend loses nothing here, since it was never his. I will grab it and split it with him!' But with buying and selling, where he cannot say this, I would say there is no oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to explain why the משנה needed to teach both cases. Here it shows what we would have wrongly thought if only the found-item case were written.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An oath is needed only where we fear a person might lie. With a found item, a dishonest person can tell himself that the other finder loses nothing real, so the temptation is strong. With a purchase, that excuse does not work, so we might have thought no oath is needed there.

keyTerms.meaning: A found item
Buying and selling, a purchase
I would have thought (a mistaken first idea)
They placed an oath on him
He excuses himself, convinces himself it is allowed

phrases.english: For if he had taught only a found item
phrases.notes: The 'he' here is the תנא, the author of the משנה.

phrases.english: I would have said:

phrases.aramaic: מְצִיאָה הוּא דִּרְמוֹ רַבָּנַן שְׁבוּעָה עֲלֵיהּ
phrases.english: it is a found item where the Rabbis placed an oath on him
because he can excuse himself and say,
'My friend loses nothing with it,'
'I will go grab it and split it with him!'
But buying and selling,
where one cannot say this –
I would say no oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the explanation of why both cases of the משנה are needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The found-item case alone would suggest the oath depends on the finder's special excuse, which does not exist in a purchase.

steps.title: If only the purchase case were taught, so both are needed
steps.stepSummary: Had the משנה taught only מקח וממכר, we would think the oath applies only there, where a buyer has his own excuse. So both cases are needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the משנה had taught only buying and selling, I would say only there did the רבנן put an oath on him. That is because he can excuse himself and say: 'My friend paid money and I paid money. Now that I need it, I will take it, and let my friend go to the trouble of buying another one.' But with a found item, where he cannot say this, I would say there is no oath. So both cases are needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the other side: what we would wrongly think if only the purchase case were taught. It ends by saying both cases are needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In a purchase, each person paid, so a dishonest buyer can tell himself, 'I paid too, my friend can just buy another.' A finder has no such excuse, so we might have thought no oath is needed for a found item. Since each case has a temptation the other lacks, neither can be learned from the other.

keyTerms.meaning: It is needed; both cases must be taught
Money, payment
To go to the trouble of buying

steps.whatToRemember: Each case in the משנה has its own reason a person might grab dishonestly: a finder thinks 'my friend loses nothing,' a buyer thinks 'my friend can buy another.' So both cases are needed.

phrases.english: And if he had taught only buying and selling,
it is there that the Rabbis placed an oath on him
because he can excuse himself and say:
'My friend is giving money'
'and I am giving money,'
'now that I need it, I will take it,'
'and let my friend go to the trouble to buy another,'
But a found item,
where one cannot say this –
I would say no oath.
So both are needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors step 1 from the other side and closes with the conclusion צריכא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The purchase case alone would suggest the oath depends on the buyer's special excuse, which a finder lacks; therefore both cases must be taught.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Both מציאה and מקח וממכר are necessary in the משנה.

steps.title: Can't we just ask the seller whose money he took?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the purchase case: why is there any doubt? Just check whose money the seller accepted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Buying and selling? Let us just see whose money the seller took!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how there could ever be a real dispute in a purchase. The seller knows whose money he took, so that person is the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller would only take money from the person he agreed to sell to. If we just check whose money he accepted, we know who the buyer is, and no oath is needed. So the case in the משנה seems not to make sense.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us see, let us check
Coins, money
He took

phrases.english: Buying and selling?
But let us see from whom he took the money!
phrases.notes: The 'he' is the seller; whoever paid him is clearly the buyer.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִקָּח וּמִמְכָּר, וְלִחְזֵי זוּזֵי מִמַּאן נָקֵט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the purchase case that step 2 relied on.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's case of a disputed purchase
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The seller's acceptance of money identifies the buyer, so there should be no doubt that needs an oath.

steps.title: The seller took money from both buyers
steps.stepSummary: The case is where the seller took money from both: one willingly and one unwillingly, and he does not remember which was which.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the case is where he took money from both of them: from one willingly, and from the other against his will. And I do not know which one was willingly and which one was against his will.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by describing a case where the seller cannot settle the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the payment the seller accepted willingly makes a sale. If he took money from both and forgot which one he really agreed to, checking the money does not help. So there is a real doubt, and the משנה's oath makes sense.

keyTerms.meaning: No, the case is needed for a situation where...
From both of them
Willingly, with his agreement
Against his will

phrases.english: No, it is needed where he took money from both of them,
from one willingly
and from one against his will,
and I do not know who is the one he took from willingly,
phrases.notes: The 'I' here is the seller speaking.

phrases.english: and who is the one against his will.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The seller took money from only one person, so there is no doubt.
steps.terutzMaskana: The seller took money from both and does not remember which payment he accepted willingly, so the doubt is real.

steps.title: Maybe our משנה does not follow בן ננס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests our משנה may disagree with בן ננס, and begins to quote him.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that our משנה is not like בן ננס? For if it were like בן ננס, doesn't he say:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic, suggesting that our משנה might not agree with the תנא בן ננס. It is setting up a quote from בן ננס that comes in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה makes both people swear, even though one of them may be lying. The גמרא is about to show that בן ננס holds a view that might clash with this. The actual quote comes in step 6, and step 7 answers the suggestion.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say (a suggestion the גמרא will test)
Our משנה
But doesn't he say

phrases.english: Shall we say our משנה is not like בן ננס?
For if it were like בן ננס, doesn't he say:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new discussion about which תנא the משנה follows.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether our משנה, which has both people swear, goes against the view of בן ננס.

steps.title: בן ננס objects to a guaranteed false oath
steps.stepSummary: The quote of בן ננס ends with his objection: how can we make both sides swear when one of them must be lying?
steps.simpleTranslation: How can these and those come to a false oath?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting בן ננס from the משנה in שבועות. This sets up the claim that our משנה might disagree with him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the case of the worker and the storekeeper, their claims clash, so one oath must be false. בן ננס refuses to require oaths there. The suggestion is that our משנה, which does require two oaths, goes against him.

keyTerms.meaning: A false or pointless oath
These and those, meaning both sides

phrases.english: How can these and those
phrases.notes: 'These and those' are the worker and the storekeeper in the משנה in שבועות that בן ננס is answering.

phrases.english: come to a false oath?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד אֵלּוּ וָאֵלּוּ בָּאִין לִידֵי שְׁבוּעַת שָׁוְא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the quote of בן ננס begun in step 5.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בן ננס holds that we do not impose oaths when one of them must be false.

steps.title: Our משנה can still fit בן ננס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the suggestion: in the worker case one oath is surely false, but in our משנה both people may have picked up the garment together.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows בן ננס. There, a false oath is certain. Here, we can say there is no false oath: maybe the two of them lifted it at the same time.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back and says our משנה does not have to disagree with בן ננס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בן ננס only objects when it is certain that one oath is a lie. In our משנה, if both lifted the garment together, each owns half, so both oaths can be true. So בן ננס would allow oaths here.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
Certainly
Together, at the same time
They lifted it

steps.confusionAlert: Each person swears he owns at least half, not the whole thing. That is why both oaths can be true at once.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows בן ננס;
there, there is certainly a false oath.
Here, one can say
that there is no false oath:
say that the two of them
lifted it together.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the suggestion that our משנה disagrees with בן ננס.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The claim that our משנה goes against בן ננס.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The worker case has a certain false oath; our case does not, since both could have lifted it together.
steps.whatToRemember: בן ננס only rejects oaths when one must be a lie. In our משנה, both may be true.

steps.title: Maybe our משנה does not follow סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests our משנה goes against סומכוס, who says doubtful money is split without any oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: Let us say our משנה is not like סומכוס. If it were, he says: money that is in doubt is divided without an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new suggestion about which תנא our משנה disagrees with.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה splits the garment but also requires an oath. סומכוס splits doubtful money with no oath at all. So it seems our משנה cannot match him.

keyTerms.meaning: Money whose owner is in doubt
They divide it

phrases.english: Let us say our משנה is not like סומכוס,
for if it were like סומכוס, doesn't he say:
money that lies in doubt
they divide without an oath.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending against בן ננס, the גמרא tests our משנה against another תנא.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does our משנה disagree with סומכוס, since it requires an oath?

steps.title: The רבנן fit even less
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: if not סומכוס, then whom, the רבנן? They say whoever wants to take money must bring proof, so they would not split it at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But then whom does it follow, the רבנן? They say: whoever wants to take money from his friend must bring proof!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the idea that our משנה is simply against סומכוס, because the other option, the רבנן, does not fit either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say doubtful money is not split; the one who wants to take it must prove his claim. Our משנה splits the garment without proof. So rejecting סומכוס leaves the משנה with no clear author.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather what? (a pushback)
The Sages who argue with סומכוס
Whoever wants to take money from another must bring proof

phrases.english: But rather what, it follows the רבנן?
But they say:
whoever takes money from his friend must bring the proof!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Pushes back on step 8 by showing the alternative to סומכוס fails too.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The simple claim that our משנה is against סומכוס and therefore follows the רבנן.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The רבנן require proof and do not split, while our משנה splits without proof.
steps.whyThisMatters: This pushback forces the גמרא to show in the next step that the רבנן's rule applies only when nobody holds the item, so our משנה fits them after all.

steps.title: The רבנן can explain our משנה well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the push from Step 9. The רבנן fit our משנה perfectly. They only require proof when neither side is holding the item. When both are holding it, they split it with an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: What kind of question is that? If you say our משנה follows the רבנן, it works: in that other case, where neither person is holding the item, the רבנן say whoever wants to take from his friend must bring proof. But here, where both are holding it, they split it with an oath.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 9 and shows that our משנה fits the רבנן without any problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 9 claimed the רבנן never split doubtful money, so our משנה could not follow them. The answer is that the rule המוציא מחבירו עליו הראיה applies only when nobody is holding the item. When both people are holding it, neither one counts as the one taking it from the other, so they split it with an oath.

keyTerms.meaning: What is this? A way of saying the comparison or question does not hold up.
Granted; this part works fine
They are holding or grasping it
Whoever wants to take money from his friend must bring proof
They split or divide it

phrases.english: What is this?
Granted, if you say it follows the Rabbis:
there, where the two of them are not holding it,
phrases.notes: 'There' is the case of doubtful money from Step 8, where nobody is holding the item.

phrases.english: the Rabbis said
whoever takes from his fellow must bring the proof;
here, where the two of them are holding it,
they divide it with an oath.
phrases.notes: The word in square brackets is part of the corrected wording.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי מַאי, אִי אָמְרַתְּ בִּשְׁלָמָא רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the push in Step 9 that the רבנן could not be the author of our משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing cases: nobody holding versus both holding
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן never split doubtful money, so our משנה cannot follow them.
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן require proof only when nobody holds the item. When both hold it, they split it with an oath.

steps.title: Why the משנה cannot follow סומכוס
steps.stepSummary: If our משנה followed סומכוס, there would be a קל וחומר problem. He splits money without an oath even when nobody holds it. So when both hold it, he should surely split it without an oath too. But our משנה requires an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if you say our משנה follows סומכוס, think about it: if in that case, where neither person is holding it, they split without an oath, then here, where both are holding it, shouldn't they all the more so split without an oath?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its point and shows why our משנה cannot follow סומכוס.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This uses a קל וחומר. Holding the item gives a person a stronger claim. If סומכוס splits without any oath even in the weaker case, he would never require an oath in the stronger case. Since our משנה does require an oath, it seems not to follow סומכוס.

keyTerms.meaning: Now, if even... (the opening of a קל וחומר)
They divide without an oath
Is it not all the more so?

phrases.english: But if you say it follows Sumchus,
now, if there,
where the two of them are not holding it,
they divide without an oath,
then here, where the two of them are holding it,
is it not all the more so!
phrases.notes: He means that here they should surely split without an oath, yet our משנה requires one.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אִי אָמְרַתְּ סוֹמְכוֹס, הַשְׁתָּא וּמָה הָתָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from Step 10. The משנה fits the רבנן, and it cannot fit סומכוס.
steps.raayaObject: Our משנה does not follow סומכוס.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A קל וחומר from סומכוס's own rule of splitting without an oath when nobody holds the item.

steps.title: סומכוס only splits without an oath when both sides are unsure
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the proof. Our משנה can follow סומכוס after all. He only splits without an oath when both sides are unsure (שמא ושמא). In our משנה each side is certain (ברי וברי), so an oath can still be required.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say our משנה follows סומכוס. סומכוס only said his rule when each side says 'maybe it is mine.' When each side says 'I am sure it is mine,' he did not say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof from Step 11 and limits סומכוס's rule to cases where both sides are unsure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר assumed סומכוס splits without an oath in every case. The גמרא now says his rule covers only שמא ושמא. In our משנה each person says 'I found it,' which is ברי וברי, so סומכוס could agree that an oath is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say
'Maybe and maybe': both sides are unsure
'Certain and certain': both sides claim to know for sure

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. In the earlier case (from Step 8), nobody knows for sure. In our משנה, each person insists he is sure. That difference is the whole answer.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Sumchus:
when Sumchus said his rule, it was for 'maybe and maybe,'
but for 'certain and certain' he did not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the קל וחומר proof of Step 11.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof that our משנה cannot follow סומכוס
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: It assumed סומכוס splits without an oath even in ברי וברי, but his rule covers only שמא ושמא.
steps.whyThisMatters: The difference between שמא ושמא and ברי וברי becomes the key to understanding how far סומכוס's rule goes.

steps.title: What about רבה בר רב הונא's view of סומכוס?
steps.stepSummary: The answer in Step 12 does not work for רבה בר רב הונא, who holds that סומכוס splits without an oath even in ברי וברי. So how could our משנה follow סומכוס according to him?
steps.simpleTranslation: But according to רבה בר רב הונא, who said סומכוס splits even when each side is certain, what can you say?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in Step 12 using רבה בר רב הונא's view, and it sets up a new answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 12 depended on limiting סומכוס to שמא ושמא. רבה בר רב הונא says סומכוס's rule also covers ברי וברי. According to him, the קל וחומר from Step 11 comes back, and the גמרא needs a different way to fit our משנה to סומכוס.

keyTerms.meaning: What is there to say? (asking for an answer to a difficulty)

phrases.english: And according to Rabbah bar Rav Huna, who said:
Sumchus said his rule even for 'certain and certain,'
what is there to say?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer of Step 12 using a different understanding of סומכוס.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer of Step 12 that limits סומכוס to שמא ושמא
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבה בר רב הונא holds that סומכוס splits without an oath even in ברי וברי, so the limit does not work and the קל וחומר of Step 11 returns.

steps.title: סומכוס only splits when there is a real money connection
steps.stepSummary: Even according to רבה בר רב הונא, our משנה can follow סומכוס. He only splits without an oath when there is a דררא דממונא, a real money connection to the item. Where there is none, as in our משנה, he does not split without an oath.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say our משנה follows סומכוס. When סומכוס said to split, he meant a case where there is a real money connection to the item. But where there is no such connection, he did not say to split.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from Step 13 with a new way our משנה can still follow סומכוס, even for רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In Step 13, the ברי/שמא answer was gone, so the גמרא needs a different line between the cases. The new line is דררא דממונא. סומכוס splits without an oath only when each side has a real money connection to the item, not just a claim. In our משנה, the two people have nothing linking them to the garment except their own claims, so סומכוס would also require an oath.

keyTerms.meaning: You can even say. This opens an answer that keeps the view we thought was ruled out.
A real money connection to the item, apart from what each side claims
In a case where there is
In a case where there is not

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think דררא דממונא just means 'there is a money argument.' Every court case has that. It means each side has a real link to the item beyond just saying 'it's mine.'
steps.whyThisMatters: דררא דממונא becomes the key idea for understanding when סומכוס splits money without an oath.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows סומכוס;
when סומכוס said to split the money,
that is where there is a real money connection to the item,
phrases.notes: Rashi reads דררא as a real money loss: whichever way the court rules wrongly, someone loses out. Each side has a real stake in the item, not just a claim.

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל הֵיכָא דְּלֵיכָּא דְּרָרָא דְמָמוֹנָא – לָא.
phrases.english: but where there is no real money connection, he did not say to split.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question from Step 13 by offering a new line between cases that works even for רבה בר רב הונא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the case: סומכוס's rule applies only where there is דררא דממונא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: For רבה בר רב הונא, סומכוס splits without an oath in every case, so our משנה, which requires an oath, cannot follow him.
steps.terutzMaskana: סומכוס splits without an oath only where there is a real money connection. Our משנה has none, so an oath fits even with סומכוס.

steps.title: Starting a new קל וחומר against the money-connection answer
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins to attack Step 14 with a קל וחומר. It starts from the case where each side has a real money connection to the item. The argument finishes on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: But isn't this a קל וחומר? If there, where this one has a real money connection and that one has a real money connection...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up a new challenge to the answer in Step 14. It starts building a קל וחומר, and the argument finishes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The קל וחומר starts from the case where סומכוס splits: both sides have a real money connection. The גמרא is about to compare that case to our משנה and argue it should come out the same way. The second half of the argument comes on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it a קל וחומר? This opens a challenge built on stronger-to-weaker logic.
If there (in that case)... This is the first half of a קל וחומר.
For this one and for that one, meaning each of the two sides

phrases.english: But isn't it a קל וחומר?
If there,
phrases.notes: 'There' means the case where סומכוס splits without an oath.
